what: The Tile Calculator works out how many tiles you need for a floor or wall. It divides the area by the space one tile takes, including the grout gap, then adds extra for cuts and breakage.
Add how many tiles come in a box and the price per box to see how many boxes to buy and the cost. It works in meters and centimeters or feet and inches.
uses: Count tiles for a kitchen, bathroom or hall.
Count tiles for a splashback or shower wall.
See how many tiles each size needs.
Get boxes and cost before you shop.
tutorial: Pick metric or imperial, then "Floor" or "Wall".
Enter length and width (or wall width and height) and any area to leave out.
Enter tile length, width and grout gap.
Pick the extra % for cuts and breakage.
Enter tiles per box and price per box (optional).
See area, tiles needed, tiles to buy, boxes and cost.
features: Each tile takes its size plus one gap.
For baths, islands, doors or windows.
Shows boxes and how many tiles are left over.
cm and mm, or inches; converts when you switch.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: A 4 × 3 m floor is 12 m². A 60 × 30 cm tile with a 3 mm gap takes 0.603 × 0.303 = 0.1827 m², so you need 12 ÷ 0.1827 = 65.7, rounded up to 66 tiles. With 10% extra that is 73 tiles. At 8 tiles per box you need 10 boxes.

tips: Measure at the widest points of the room.
Large tiles and diagonal layouts need more extra.
Keep a few spare tiles for future repairs.
Check the box label for coverage per box as a cross-check.
